MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 84
   B. 83
   C. 86
   D. 85

2. Which Roman numeral stands for 7? (1 mark)
   A. VIIII
   B. IIII
   C. VX
   D. VII

3. Which list shows all the factors of 42? (1 mark)
   A. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   B. 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21
   C. 1, 2, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   D. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42

4. Which of these is a factor of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 3
   C. 25
   D. 4

5. Which of these is a factor of 45? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 9
   C. 2
   D. 6

6. Work out 2,450 + 3,875. (1 mark)
   A. 6,225
   B. 6,335
   C. 5,225
   D. 6,325

7. Which sum checks that 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225? (1 mark)
   A. 5,225 − 3,275
   B. 5,225 + 3,275
   C. 8,500 + 3,275
   D. 8,500 + 5,225

8. Work out 19 × 31. (1 mark)
   A. 589
   B. 599
   C. 76
   D. 579

9. What is 35 × 60? (1 mark)
   A. 2,100
   B. 21,000
   C. 210
   D. 95

10. What is 78 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 13
   B. 12
   C. 14
   D. 23

11. What is 63 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 22
   B. 20
   C. 21
   D. 31

12. What is 500 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 50
   C. 6
   D. 500

13. 59 mangoes are shared equally among 8 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 4
   C. 3
   D. 5

14. What is 4/9 of 27? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 15
   C. 13
   D. 12

15. Change 3 3/4 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 12/4
   B. 16/4
   C. 6/4
   D. 15/4

16. In the fraction 7/10, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 17
   C. 3
   D. 10

17. Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5/5
   B. 15/5
   C. 18/5
   D. 17/5

18. In the number 8.30, the digit 3 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tenths
   C. Tens
   D. Hundredths

19. Write 3 1/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 3.1
   B. 3.01
   C. 31.0
   D. 0.31

20. A hundred square has 5 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 0.005
   C. 0.05
   D. 0.5

21. Write 5 7/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 5.07
   B. 5.7
   C. 5.007
   D. 57.0

22. Simplify 3a + 2a. (1 mark)
   A. 6a
   B. 5aa
   C. 5a
   D. 5

23. Wairimu had d shillings and spent 45 shillings. Which expression shows the money she has left? (1 mark)
   A. 45 − d
   B. 45d
   C. d − 45
   D. d + 45

24. Change 3 m to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3 cm
   B. 30 cm
   C. 300 cm
   D. 3,000 cm

25. Change 640 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 40 cm
   B. 64 cm
   C. 6 m 90 cm
   D. 7 m 40 cm

26. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 2 m 50 cm
   B. 3 m 50 cm
   C. 25 cm
   D. 3 m

27. A rectangle is made of 11 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 32 square units
   B. 55 square units
   C. 16 square units
   D. 66 square units

28. How many 5 L buckets can be filled from a 20 L jerrycan? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 4
   C. 15
   D. 5

29. What is 2 1/4 kg + 1 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 kg
   B. 4 1/4 kg
   C. 3 1/2 kg
   D. 3 3/4 kg

30. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 6 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 6:45
   B. 7:30
   C. 6:06
   D. 6:30

31. When is a shadow shortest? (1 mark)
   A. Around midday
   B. Late in the afternoon
   C. Early in the morning
   D. At night

32. 450 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 5.50
   B. Ksh 0.45
   C. Ksh 45
   D. Ksh 4.50

33. A customer pays with Ksh 2,000 for goods that cost Ksh 1,340. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 660
   B. Ksh 3,340
   C. Ksh 760
   D. Ksh 650

34. 75 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 0.07
   B. Ksh 7.50
   C. Ksh 0.75
   D. Ksh 1.75

35. What do we call the point where the two arms of an angle meet? (1 mark)
   A. The edge
   B. The vertex
   C. The arm
   D. The side

36. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with three equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 1

37. Which statement about a square is true? (1 mark)
   A. Its opposite sides are different
   B. All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   C. It has only three corners
   D. It has no lines of symmetry

38. How many lines of symmetry does an oval have? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 2
   C. 1
   D. 0

39. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are NOT car? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 9
   C. 1
   D. 10

40. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many more are there of mango than of banana? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 2
   C. 7
   D. 1

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write 2 25/100 and 5 7/100 as decimals. (2 marks)

42. Explain why we should change lengths to centimetres before adding 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

43. The minute hand of a clock points to 4 and the hour hand is just past 9. What time is it? Explain how you know. (3 marks)

44. Otieno is a years old and his sister is 3 years older. Write an expression for his sister's age and find her age if Otieno is 9. (3 marks)

45. Mr Otieno has Ksh 2,000. He buys items costing Ksh 1,340. Does he have enough money? How much is left? (3 marks)

46. A square garden has sides of 15 m. Find the perimeter of the garden. (2 marks)

47. Explain what a right angle is. State how many right angles there are in (a) a rectangle, (b) a straight line, (c) a full turn. (5 marks)

48. Explain how you can use a beam balance to find the mass of a bag of sugar. (3 marks)

49. A bus carried 5,684 passengers on Saturday and 3,749 on Sunday. Find the total number of passengers and check your answer by adding in the opposite order. (4 marks)

50. Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest. (3 marks)

51. Write the first five multiples of 9. (2 marks)

52. A bicycle costs Ksh 6,500, a helmet Ksh 1,750 and a lock Ksh 850. Find the total cost. (3 marks)

53. Work out 12 × 21 showing both partial products. (3 marks)

54. Explain why you should read a measuring jug at the same height as the water. (2 marks)

55. Wangari buys 24 exercise books at Ksh 18 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding to the nearest ten, then work out the exact cost. (4 marks)

56. Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she study in all? (3 marks)

57. Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule. (3 marks)

58. Nanjala says an angle with longer arms is always bigger. Is she right? Explain. (3 marks)

59. Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule. (3 marks)

60. On a poultry farm each of 16 hens lays 21 eggs in one month. How many eggs are laid altogether? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 84
   84 = 12 × 7, so 84 is a multiple of 12.

2. D — VII
   7 is written VII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

3. A — 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42
   Pair up numbers that multiply to 42. The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42.

4. C — 25
   50 ÷ 25 = 2 with nothing left over, so 25 is a factor of 50. The others leave a remainder.

5. B — 9
   45 ÷ 9 = 5 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 45. The others leave a remainder.

6. D — 6,325
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

7. B — 5,225 + 3,275
   Addition undoes subtraction. 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500, the starting number.

8. A — 589
   19 × 1 = 19 and 19 × 30 = 570. 19 + 570 = 589.

9. A — 2,100
   35 × 6 = 210, then × 10 gives 2,100.

10. A — 13
   6 × 13 = 78, so 78 ÷ 6 = 13.

11. C — 21
   3 × 21 = 63, so 63 ÷ 3 = 21.

12. A — 5
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 500 ÷ 100 = 5.

13. C — 3
   59 ÷ 8 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

14. D — 12
   27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 3 × 4 = 12. So 4/9 of 27 is 12.

15. D — 15/4
   3 × 4 = 12 and 12 + 3 = 15. The denominator stays 4, so the answer is 15/4.

16. D — 10
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

17. D — 17/5
   3 × 5 = 15 and 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 5, so the answer is 17/5.

18. B — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 8.30 the digit 3 is in the tenths place.

19. A — 3.1
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3 1/10 = 3.1.

20. C — 0.05
   5 out of 100 squares is 5/100 = 0.05.

21. A — 5.07
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5 7/100 = 5.07.

22. C — 5a
   Only like terms can be joined. 3a + 2a = 5a.

23. C — d − 45
   Spent means take away, so she has d − 45 left.

24. C — 300 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 3 × 100 = 300. So the answer is 300 cm.

25. A — 6 m 40 cm
   640 ÷ 100 = 6 remainder 40. So 640 cm = 6 m 40 cm.

26. A — 2 m 50 cm
   250 ÷ 100 = 2 remainder 50. So 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm.

27. B — 55 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 11 × 5 = 55 square units.

28. B — 4
   20 ÷ 5 = 4 buckets.

29. D — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 2 1/4 kg + 1 1/2 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

30. D — 6:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 6:30.

31. A — Around midday
   At midday the Sun is highest, so shadows are very short.

32. D — Ksh 4.50
   450 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 50, so it is Ksh 4.50.

33. A — Ksh 660
   Change = amount paid − cost = 2,000 − 1,340 = Ksh 660.

34. C — Ksh 0.75
   75 ÷ 100 = 0 remainder 75, so it is Ksh 0.75.

35. B — The vertex
   The arms of an angle meet at a point called the vertex.

36. C — 3
   Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side.

37. B — All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

38. B — 2
   An oval folds along its length and across its width.

39. B — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

40. D — 1
   4 − 3 = 1.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2.25 and 5.07
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal. 5 7/100 needs a 0 in the tenths place.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: When both lengths are in centimetres we can add them like ordinary numbers: 345 + 280 = 625 cm. This avoids mistakes with regrouping 100 cm into 1 m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using one unit, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for reference to regrouping.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9:20. Each number is worth 5 minutes, so the minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9:20, 1 mark for 5 minutes per number, 1 mark for 4 × 5.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: a + 3. When a = 9, her age is 12 years.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a + 3, 1 mark for replacing a by 9, 1 mark for 12 years.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Yes. He has Ksh 660 left.
   Working / marking points: 2,000 is more than 1,340 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,340 (1 mark); Ksh 660 (1 mark).

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60 m
   Working / marking points: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m. 1 mark for method and 1 mark for answer with unit.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: A right angle is a square corner, made by a quarter turn. (a) 4 (b) 2 (c) 4
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for explaining a right angle (square corner or quarter turn), 1 mark for each of (a) 4, (b) 2 and (c) 4.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the sugar in one pan. Add known masses to the other pan until the beam is level. Add up the masses to find the mass of the sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for putting the sugar in a pan, 1 mark for adding known masses until level, 1 mark for adding the masses.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: 9,433 passengers. Check: 3,749 + 5,684 = 9,433.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct working with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with unit, 1 mark for the check.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 506, 560, 605, 650
   Working / marking points: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 9,100
   Working / marking points: 6,500 + 1,750 = 8,250 (1 mark); 8,250 + 850 (1 mark); Ksh 9,100 (1 mark).

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 252
   Working / marking points: 12 × 1 = 12 (1 mark); 12 × 20 = 240 (1 mark); 12 + 240 = 252 (1 mark).

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Looking from above or below makes the water level seem to be at a different mark, so the reading would be wrong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the reading can be wrong and 1 mark for the reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 20 × 20 = 400. Exact: 24 × 18 = 432 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 400, 1 mark for the exact working (24 × 8 = 192 and 24 × 10 = 240), 1 mark for 432.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 5 minutes
   Working / marking points: 20 + 45 = 65 min (1 mark); 1 h + 65 min = 2 h 5 min (2 marks).

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 250, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250. Rule: add 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: No. The size of an angle depends on how far apart the arms are, not on how long they are.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for no, 1 mark for the opening between the arms, 1 mark for length not mattering.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,500, 2,500, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500. Rule: add 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: 336 eggs
   Working / marking points: 21 × 6 = 126 (1 mark); 21 × 10 = 210 (1 mark); 126 + 210 = 336 (1 mark).
